newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS-Supply stirs despite rate rise.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS-Supply stirs despite rate rise.

text.p: Corporate debt supply continues to stir despite higher interest rates and a load of new supply coming from the U.S. government market, dealers said.
Raytheon Co's highly anticipated $2.5 billion debt offering will be the focus in the market this week; however, other names are gearing up as well, players said.
The defense contractor's offering, currently in roadshow, is rumored to be increased in size with the possibility of additional tranches added, players said.
"We're hearing that the deal may be upped in size and three- and -20-year tranches may be added," said one dealer.
Raytheon spokesperson Robert McWade had no comment on the market rumors but said the completion of the deal was targeted for close of business on Thursday.
The current breakdown on the debt offering, which will be underwritten by Morgan Stanley Dean Witter, is as follows, dealers said.
-- $1.0 billion five-year debt, unofficial price talk seen between 40-45 basis points over U.S. Treasuries,
Another $400 million is expected from Meditrust Healthcare, $200 million via Staples Inc, and $100 million from Summit Properties, sources said.
In the broader market, secondary high grade trading was subdued with spreads remaining unchanged across most maturities, players said.
Players were said to be closely watching the bulk of new government supply already coming in, hoping good auctions will serve to bolster recently weaker Treasury prices.
Treasuries suffered steep declines last Friday following stronger-than-expected U.S. employment and manufacturing data.
-- $1.0 billion 10-year debt, unofficial price talk seen between 60-65 basis points over Treasuries,
-- $500 million 30-year debt, unofficial price talk seen between 75-80 basis points over Treasuries.
Among other names, Amoco Corp, a major integrated oil firm, is slated to bring $200 million in a 10-year debt offering via Morgan Stanley Dean Witter, sources said.
In addition, Morgan Stanley is expected to underwrite a $150 million 30-year debt offering for textile producer Burlington Industries, sources said.
The T-bond closed off 6/32 at 101-23/32 to yield 6.49 pct.
Meanwhile, the U.S. Treasury sold $16 billion in three-year notes on Tuesday producing average yields of 6.041 percent, slightly higher than anticipated.
But most players are concentrating on Wednesday's sale of $12 billion in 10-year notes. Another $10 billion in 30-year bonds will hit the market on Thursday.
Elsewhere, junk bond prices ended mixed in moderate trading volume, players said.
Grand Union 12 percent debt gained one full point to close at 47-1/2 bid, 49 offer, players said.

New junk supply featured High Voltage Engineering's $135 million sale of seven-year debt at 10.50 percent. The issue, which priced at par, traded up on the break to 100-1/2 bid, 100-3/4 offer, players said. The firm also sold $35 million in 10-year senior redeemable securities at +627 basis points.

Other offerings expected for later in the week include a $200 million offering from ICN Pharmaceuticals Inc, $320 million Euro/144a offering from MRS Logistica SA and a $200 million 10-year deal from Signature Resorts Inc, sources said.
